newsitem.title: UK: Flextech, BBC agree pay TV joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Flextech, BBC agree pay TV joint venture.

text.p: Flextech Plc, a unit of Telecommunications International Inc (Tinta), said on Monday it would form a joint venture with BBC Worldwide Limited to create pay television channels for the UK.
In a statement it said a parallel agreement had been reached between Discovery Inc, a sister company to Tinta, and BBC Worldwide to develop channels for the U.S. and other markets.
Flextech said final details of the deal were expected to be agreed by the end of this year.
It said the first Flextech-BBC Worldwide channels might launch as early as summer of 1997.
The venture would include documentaries, natural history, drama, comedy, lifestyle, arts, music and learning.
The BBC had also been approached by satellite broadcaster BSkyB, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is the largest shareholder.
Flextech said today's announcement extended its existing venture with BBC Worldwide, who are co-shareholders in cable television channel UK Gold along with Pearson Plc and Cox Communications.
Cox and Tele-Communications Inc are the major shareholders in Discovery.
Flextech chief executive Roger Luard said in a statement that the deal wolud "produce exiting television that will have wide appeal for multichannel audiences."

"The task ahead of us is to continue our discussions with players in the sector and arrange distribution for our new channels over satellite and cable systems," said Bob Phillis, chief executive of BBC Worldwide.
